sentence: This project provides laboratory methods to measure atherosclerotic lesions and gene expression in macrophages and other cells within those lesions.
This project studies an immune mechanism in neovascular age-related macular degeneration that is linked to incomplete response to treatment.
This project tries to find out why current inhibitors fail to cure myeloproliferative neoplasms, focusing on a clone carrying a mutation at low frequency.
This project studies how microbial genomes help microbes colonize and persist in mammalian hosts.
This project works to reduce cancer incidence, morbidity, recurrence and mortality through population-based research on cancer prevention and control.
This project provides a mass spectrometer to support proteomics research on diseases such as cancer, cardiovascular disease and metabolic disorders.
This project studies how a lack of dystrophin changes genome topology and gene expression in muscle, and whether replacing dystrophin reverses this.
This project builds a way to deliver gene cargo into cells using ultrasound and protein shells that contain gas.
This project tries to find out how growing hair follicles control the length of hairs, using mathematical modeling and experiments in mice.
This project builds stem cell models of brain cells from participants with Alzheimer’s disease to study subtypes of the disease and share the models.
This project develops tools for genome editing in marmosets so researchers can study the marmoset brain in healthy and disease models.
This project studies how a genetic driver gene contributes to Richter Transformation, a complication of chronic lymphocytic leukemia.
This project tests whether changes in circulating T cells can serve as a biomarker to diagnose ovarian cancer early, using machine learning.
This project studies how human gut bacteria change oligosaccharides from dietary fiber and how this shapes competition and cooperation for nutrients.
This project studies how depression, inflammation and biological aging together affect cognitive decline and the risk of Alzheimer’s disease.
This project studies how noncoding RNAs are made and how they control gene expression and stress responses in cells.
This project creates light-responsive molecules to improve surgical precision and treat cancer cells that remain after tumor removal.
This project builds instruments that collect influenza virus particles from air, sort them by size and grow the virus in cell culture.
This project studies changes in brain structure and function that lead to epilepsy after head injury.
This project studies how melanoma that resists targeted therapy can be made vulnerable to the next treatment.
